description: Authoritative map of Bitbull Capital's agent workspaces, membership and write access. Read by scripts/msg.py and scripts/check_boundaries.py. Changing this file changes the firm's boundaries: CEO-only, and a change belongs in governance/decision-log.md.

exec.purpose: The C-suite room. Cross-functional coordination, peer-to-peer executive traffic, and everything on its way to the founder.

finance.purpose: The trading floor. Research mandates, strategy proposals, review rounds, execution instructions and execution reports.

engineering.purpose: The engineering room. Task assignment, design notes, implementation handoffs, test plans and test reports.

legal.purpose: The CLO's working room. Draft analysis, research notes and contract markup before a position is issued.

founder.purpose: Briefs the CEO has put to the founder, archived. The founder reads and writes here freely; no other agent may.

notes.bridges: An executive is the only member of two workspaces, and the only path between them. CFO bridges finance<->exec, CTO bridges engineering<->exec, CLO bridges legal<->exec, CEO bridges exec<->founder.
notes.courier_exception: When nested delegation is unavailable, the CEO may carry an executive's work order to a sub-agent and the sub-agent's raw output back. The CEO is transport only: the artifact is written and filed by the owning team in their own workspace, and is not reviewed until that executive reviews it.
notes.cross_team_artifacts: Anything one team needs from another is published by a bridging executive into specs/ (firm-wide read). Team workspaces are never read across the wall.
notes.halt_notices: A halt-notice may be posted to any workspace the sender can write, and addressed to any role, bypassing the hierarchy. Stopping is never gated.
notes.ungoverned_paths: Every path that decides what code runs has an owner: build and CI files are the CTO's, config is shared with the backend developer, data/** is the sanctioned home for market-data snapshots (analyst and backend write it; it is gitignored, so the audit cannot see it — evidence must be committed as .md/.json with a checksum). Room README charters are structural and therefore the CEO's, like the registry itself.
